title: The Sixteenth Semester
premise: Kestrel Nakamura has spent three years keeping their family invisible while their mother works hospital night shifts, so when an anonymous group chat called the Sixteenth Semester starts posting predictions that come true — a fire drill, a teacher's resignation, a classmate's accident — Kestrel is furious to find themselves named in it. The chat's messages turn out to be fragments of a buried school board report about a decades-old cover-up that explains why their neighborhood school keeps losing funding, and why Kestrel's late grandmother, a former student, left behind a box of documents no one would explain. As the predictions escalate toward 'the final audition' — a district showcase the board plans to use as a photo-op — Kestrel must choose between staying safely unseen and going public with the truth, dragging their siblings into the line of fire. In the end, Kestrel leaks the report during the audition itself, forcing the board's resignation, and discovers the chat was created by their grandmother's old classmates finishing what she started.
about_author: Coral Underhill is the pen name of a former substitute teacher who grew up in a rust-belt school district slated for consolidation. They write stories about kids who hold families together and refuse to be overlooked.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A day in the life: packing lunches for siblings Milo and June, acing a chemistry quiz, deflecting a counselor's questions about 'home support.' Establishes the family's fragile routine and Kestrel's rule of invisibility. Emotional beat: pride in competence shadowed by exhaustion and the fear that one misstep could unravel everything.

chapters.title: The Invitation Nobody Sent
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A strange notification appears: added to a group chat called the Sixteenth Semester, populated by accounts with no faces. The first message predicts tomorrow's fire drill to the minute — and it happens exactly. Kestrel tells no one, but can't delete the chat. Emotional beat: unease curdling into obsession; the watcher realizes they are being watched.

chapters.title: Named
chapters.summary: Alternating Kestrel and Milo POV. The chat posts a prediction naming Kestrel: 'The eldest will find what was hidden in the green box.' That night Kestrel opens their grandmother's untouched storage box and finds a 1998 district report with pages redacted. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing; the past stops being past.

chapters.title: Rules of the Roster
chapters.summary: June's POV. June, twelve and fearless, decodes the chat's pattern: every prediction maps onto dates from grandma's yearbook. Meanwhile at school, a beloved teacher abruptly resigns — another prediction fulfilled. Kestrel forbids the younger kids from digging. Emotional beat: sibling friction; protection beginning to feel like control.

chapters.title: What the Board Buried
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Research montage: the redacted report concerns lead contamination in the annex building and a settlement that paid for silence, not repairs. Grandma Nakamura was one of the students who got sick. The chat posts its most chilling message yet: 'The final audition will not go as planned.' Emotional beat: cold clarity — this isn't a prank, it's a case file.

chapters.title: Detention for the Innocent
chapters.summary: Milo's POV. Milo is suspended for a vandalism he didn't commit after asking questions in class — retaliation, clearly. Mom, working doubles, can't come in; Kestrel handles the hearing alone and loses. Emotional beat: rage and helplessness; the system isn't broken, it's functioning exactly as designed.

chapters.title: The Other Members
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Following the yearbook trail, Kestrel finds one of grandma's surviving classmates, Mr. Okafor, now the school's night custodian. He admits he helped seed the chat with the report's contents to force the truth out before the board demolishes the records. Emotional beat: wary alliance; inheritance reframed as a relay baton, not a burden.

chapters.title: Escalation
chapters.summary: June's POV. The board announces the annex will be demolished the week after the district showcase — the 'final audition' — destroying all physical evidence. The chat goes silent. June secretly copies the report files; Kestrel catches her, and they finally work together instead of against each other. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve; the siblings become a team.

chapters.title: The Final Audition
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. At the showcase, with cameras rolling and the superintendent mid-speech, Kestrel takes the stage under pretense of the student performance and reads the unredacted findings aloud, projecting the documents behind them. Chaos, then a hush as Mr. Okafor and other alumni stand in solidarity. Emotional beat: terror becoming voice; invisibility abandoned on purpose.

chapters.title: Semester's End
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, weeks later. Two board members resign, remediation is ordered, and the chat sends its last message: 'Class dismissed,' signed with grandma's initials among four others. Kestrel, no longer hiding, applies for the debate team; Milo's suspension is expunged. Emotional beat: quiet triumph — justice arrived outside the law, and Kestrel learned that being seen is survivable.
